newsitem.title: USA: Brent cargoes seen headed to U.S. Gulf Coast.
newsitem.headline: Brent cargoes seen headed to U.S. Gulf Coast.

text.p: Foreign crude traders in the U.S. said Monday they expect to see a pair of North Sea Brent cargoes heading to the U.S. Gulf Coast despite a narrow Atlantic arbitrage.
At the same time, a Wall Street trader confirmed it sold one of two Brent cargoes late last week at 10 cts below October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for early October delivery.
The same trader said it was in possession of the two fresh Brent cargoes, "but was not sure what we'll be doing with them."
Overall, traders said North Sea business has been muted by the arbitrage, which stood at $1.10-$1.15 for November and at $1.00-$1.05 for December.
Dated Brent declined sharply Monday, with a Sept 20-22 Brent sold to a U.K. refiner at Oct Brent less 47 cts, 12-15 cts weaker than last trades Thursday.
Paper Brent was dealt in the U.S. aftermarket window for Oct/Nov at plus 43 cts, 44 cts and 45 cts, weakening 30-40 cts from Friday's closing levels.
Nov/Dec Brent paper was also lower, trading at 50 cts Monday, some 20 cts lower.
In Latin America, business for the most part was subdued. There was market talk that a major was heard offering Cusiana at November WTI minus 10 cents for mid-October.
That same major was also heard offering Canadian parcels for Koch Alberta at Oct WTI minus $1.00 for mid-October.
Traders were also discussing offers for Qua Iboe at Nov WTI plus 40 cents, also for mid-October delivery.
